reasons: The cited Section 13 contains a Vendor-to-Customer (Garman → Sparkling) IP indemnity: an express ownership/non-infringement warranty coupled with an indemnity for all Losses (settlements, legal fees, investigation costs) arising from breach of that warranty, plus the customary infringement remedy ladder (procure right, procure equivalent, replace/modify). Direction of the obligation is correct and there is no reverse one-way Customer indemnity, so walk-away territory does not arise.

This satisfies the rule's fallback position (Vendor IP indemnity with usual remedies), and Section 15 expressly carves Section 13 out of the direct-damages-only and consequential-damages limitations, leaving the indemnity uncapped — better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. Under the playbook's classification semantics a clause at the fallback is compliant and should not be redlined.

The failed deterministic check is adequately explained as a phrasing/proximity artefact: the indemnity verb and the word 'infringement' appear in the same paragraph but beyond the quote window, and the trigger is drafted as breach of the ownership warranty rather than the literal phrase 'infringement claim'.

Shortfalls versus the preferred position (no express 'defend'/control-of-defence and cooperation mechanic, no refund/termination remedy, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross-negligence limbs, affiliates not named, tight ten-day notice) are correctly recorded in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than escalated as deviations.
No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is consistent with a compliant finding retained as internal evidence.
